newsitem.title: USA: Caterpillar sees 1997 sales slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar sees 1997 sales slightly up.

text.p: Caterpillar Inc said Tuesday it expects 1997 sales to be up slightly from an expected record in 1996.
"Our preliminary outlook for 1997 is to slightly surpass the record levels achieved in 1996," chairman and chief executive officer Donald Fites said in a news release.
Higher industry demand in developing regions, Canada and Australia are expected to offset slightly lower industry demand in the United States, Europe and Japan, the heavy equipment maker said.

"We continue to see opportunities for solid growth in the vast majority of the global markets we serve, particularly in the fast-growing developing nations where infrastructure needs are greatest," Fites said.
The company's current record sales year was 1995, with $16.07 billion in sales.
The company also said it expects profit in 1996 to exceed the 1995 level of $1.14 billion.
For the industry, worldwide demand for engines is forecast to decline from last year's record levels, while industry machine sales are projected near last year's levels, Caterpillar said.
U.S. machine demand is seen slightly below 1995 levels, while truck engine demand is expected to decline noticeably, Caterpillar said.
In Europe, demand is expected to decline from last year due to expected gross domestic product growth below two percent.

Higher industry demand is seen in 1996 in Asia, China, Africa and the Middle East. Moderate economic growth in Australia and Japan should result in slightly higher industry demand, but Latin America will decline despite a stronger economy, Caterpillar said.

In 1997, worldwide industry demand for engines is expected to increase, despite lower truck demand from original equipment manufacturers in North America, Caterpillar said, adding that commercial engine demand should be higher both inside and outside North America.
Caterpillar shares rose 1-3/4 to 75-7/8 early Tuesday.
